item.title: Square-root cancellation in three hyperbolic counting problems via maximal estimates
item.description: arXiv:2611.26738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study three counting problems for lattice orbits in hyperbolic space: counting orbit points within a prescribed distance of a fixed closed geodesic or a totally geodesic hyperplane, and counting orbit points above a prescribed height at a cusp. For almost every base point, we obtain error bounds of square-root size up to logarithmic factors. For the geodesic and hyperplane counts, these bounds match the conjectured exponents and improve earlier results due to Good and Laaksonen. For these two problems, we adapt the method of maximal estimates developed by Chatzakos and Dimakis for hyperbolic lattice counting, formulating it in both a discrete and a continuous framework. For the hyperplane problem, we also obtain an asymptotic formula for the spatial second moment of the error term, involving an almost periodic function. For the cusp problem, the square-root bound can be deduced from work of Yu, which incorporates Schmidt's dyadic maximal argument. We present a proof, together with an $\Omega$-result supporting the optimality of the exponent $1/2$ for at least one cusp of any group that is not essentially cuspidal. In contrast, for the modular group, we obtain a power saving over the exponent $1/2$ for every base point.
item.dc:creator: Marios Voskou

item.title: On generation of the coefficient field of a primitive HMF by a single Fourier coefficient: An application of Nekov\'a\v{r}'s Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.26934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be a non-CM primitive Hilbert modular form (HMF) over a totally real number field, of parallel even weight $k\geq 2$, with coefficient field $E_f$, and let $F_f \subseteq E_f$ denote the field fixed by the inner twists of $f$. In this article, we establish an analogue of Ribet's large image theorem for the residual Galois representations associated with $f$, by applying Nekov\'a\v{r}'s large image theorem (cf.~\cite[Theorem B.5.2]{Nek12}) to the automorphic representation $\pi(f)$ associated with $f$. As a result, we prove that if $f$ has no nontrivial inner twists, then $E_f$ is generated by a single prime Fourier coefficient, for a set of prime ideals of Dirichlet density one. We derive this result as a consequence of a more general theorem established for $F_f$.
item.dc:creator: Narasimha Kumar, Dwipanjana Shit

item.title: An explicit Cassels--Tate pairing in characteristic $2$ and the parity of $2$-Selmer ranks
item.description: arXiv:2611.27040v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a global field of characteristic $2$ and $\varphi\colon E\to E'$ the Verschiebung of an ordinary elliptic curve $E/K$ with a rational point of order $2$. We prove an explicit formula for the homogeneous-space Cassels--Tate pairing on $\Sha(E/K)[\varphi]$ as a sum of local Artin--Schreier symbols, show that it coincides with Kramer's descent pairing and, on $\Sha(E/K)[\varphi]$, with the pairing induced by Milne's flat duality, and deduce that it is non-degenerate on $\Sha(E/K)[\varphi]/\hat\varphi(\Sha(E'/K)[2])$. For every ordinary elliptic curve $A/K$ we express the parity of $\mathrm{rk}\,A(K)+\dim\Sha(A/K)[2]$ by local terms (after Kramer), and identify these with local root numbers at places of semistable or potentially multiplicative reduction, and in further cases using curves with finite $\Sha$. We determine $\Sha$ in examples, and extend the formula to rational points of any prime order $\ell$, the new case being $\ell=\operatorname{char}K$.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Shukla

item.title: Half-integrality and an upper bound for slopes of Drinfeld cuspforms of level $\Gamma_1(t^r)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.27291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be a rational prime, let $q>1$ be a power of $p$ and let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be the field of $q$ elements. Let $k\geq 2$ and $r\geq 1$ be integers. Let $S_k(\Gamma_1(t^r))$ be the $\mathbb{C}_\infty$-vector space of Drinfeld cuspforms of rank two, level $\Gamma_1(t^r)$ and weight $k$ over $\mathbb{F}_q(t)$. In this paper, we prove that every finite $t$-adic slope of the Hecke operator $U_t$ on $S_k(\Gamma_1(t^r))$ belongs to $\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}$ and is at most $k-2$. If $q$ is odd, then every such slope is an integer.
item.dc:creator: Shin Hattori

item.title: The geometric expansion of the coarse trace formula of GL(4)
item.description: arXiv:2611.27310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the non-semisimple terms in the geometric side of Arthur's trace formula of $\rm{GL}(4)$ for the further study of the invariant trace formula. After modifying the zeta function and Arthur's definition of the weighted orbital integrals, we compare the two ways to calculate the distributions $J^T(f)$ of the geometric side, we can obtain that the distributions can be written as the linear combanition of the weighted orbital integrals. In particular, we get the coefficients $a^M(S,\gamma)$, for all $\gamma\in \rm{GL}(4,F)$, expressed by the measure and zeta functions.
item.dc:creator: Haoyang Wang, Xinghua Cui, Weilong Zhang, Zhifeng Peng

item.title: Lower bounds for mixed moments of modular and Dirichlet $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.27431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be a fixed holomorphic Hecke cusp form of level one. For every fixed positive integer $k$, we prove a lower bound of order $q(\log q)^{2k^2}$ for the $2k$-th moment of $L(1/2,f\otimes\chi)L(1/2,\chi)$ over primitive characters modulo a sufficiently large prime $q$.
item.dc:creator: Yu Hao Qiu, Nanxiang Wang

item.title: Regular quadratic lattices are rare over real quadratic fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.27574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a positive definite regular quadratic lattice of rank at least 4 over a totally real number field contains a regular sublattice that represents precisely the totally positive integers lying in an ideal. Under the generalized Riemann hypothesis and a conjecture on class numbers, it follows that, for each $m$, real quadratic fields admitting a positive definite regular lattice of some rank between 4 and $m$ have density 0. Unconditionally, only finitely many real quadratic fields of narrow class number 1 admit a positive definite regular lattice of some rank between 4 and 7.
item.dc:creator: Vitezslav Kala, Dayoon Park

item.title: Generalized Markov numbers and plane lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.27627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give new explicit constructions of lattice rules in the two-dimensional square and torus. It is well-known that uniformly distributed lattices (in the sense of low-discrepancy) arise from continued fractions with bounded partial denominators. We demonstrate how integers solutions of the generalized Markov equation $x^2+y^2+z^2 = kxyz-k+3$ give rise to such lattices.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Nagel, Friedrich Pillichshammer

item.title: Splitting types of Richelot isogenies over finite fields and a newform of weight four
item.description: arXiv:2611.27775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A factorization $f=uvw$ of a square-free sextic over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ of odd characteristic into three monic quadratics defines a genus-2 curve with a rational $(2,2)$-isogeny kernel, and the Richelot construction attaches to it three dual quadratics $U,V,W$. We determine, for every odd prime power $q$, the number of such factorizations with prescribed splitting behaviour over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of all six quadratics. Each of the $64$ counts is $q(q-1)(q+1-n_f)/64$ times $C(q)\pm t_q$, where $n_f$ is the number of roots of $f$ in $\mathbb{F}_q$, $C$ is an explicit monic cubic, and $t_q$ is the trace of Frobenius attached to the newform $\eta(2z)^{4}\eta(4z)^{4}$ of weight $4$ and level $8$. The proof reduces the counts by elementary means to a twisted second moment of the Legendre family of elliptic curves, which is a value of a hypergeometric function over $\mathbb{F}_q$ evaluated by Ahlgren and Ono for primes. As consequences, the number of factorizations whose three pairwise resultants lie in one square class is a polynomial in $q$, with proportion $1/4+3/(4q^{2})+O(q^{-4})$. When the quotient is a product of two elliptic curves conjugate over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$, we prove that the splitting of the factors $u,v,w$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ decides which points of order two of the elliptic factor are divisible by two.
item.dc:creator: Hung Dang

item.title: An arithmetic theory of simultaneous rational-translation Lagrange equality spectra
item.description: arXiv:2611.27825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show geometric and dimensional properties of simultaneous rational-translation Lagrange equality spectra for both $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}}$ and $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(\delta)}$ using the projective cocycle steering method, which we introduce. In particular, we show the existence of a simultaneous Hall ray for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}}$, a simultaneous Hall interval for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(\delta)}$, regimes of full and positive Hausdorff dimension, a scaling law, empty low spectra in certain cases, a compact set of full Hausdorff dimension in $(2Q\sqrt 3 - \varepsilon, 2Q\sqrt 3)$ where $Q$ is a common denominator of the finite set of rationals giving the translations, and the density of Lagrange equality sets in $\mathbb{R}$ for Lagrange constants in the Hall ray or Hall interval, respectively. Furthermore, we show that the Lagrange equality set for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}}$, for a finite set of rational translations, is thick but, for the set of all rational translations, is empty. Likewise, we bound the Hausdorff dimension of the Lagrange equality sets for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(\delta)}$ in every nonempty open interval of $\mathbb{R}$. For each fixed $Q$, our result on the Hall interval, the density result, and the dimension bounds for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(\delta)}$ hold for all sufficiently small $\delta>0$. Both emptiness results (low spectra and the Lagrange equality set under all rational translations) hold for every $\delta>0$.
item.dc:creator: Jimmy Tseng

item.title: Cobham theorem for expansive bases in orders of number fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.27882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a Cobham theorem for bases $\alpha,\beta$ in the ring of integers $R$ of a number field $K$ of degree $d\ge 2$, the bases being expansive, that is, of absolute value greater than $1$ at every archimedean place. The two required conditions are $\mathbb Q(\alpha^r,\beta^s)=K$ and $\alpha^r R\ne\beta^s R$ for all $r,s\ge 1$. Under these conditions, a function from $R$ to a finite alphabet is automatic in both bases if and only if it is eventually periodic, that is, if it agrees, outside a finite set, with a function periodic for a subgroup of $R$ of rank $d$. Both conditions are necessary: if either fails, some subset of $R$ is automatic in both bases without being eventually periodic. The proof distinguishes bases with different and with equal prime-ideal supports, using recognisability of constant-shape substitutions and comparisons of exact affine symmetries. The result extends to arbitrary orders, to lattices stable under the bases, and to suitable pairs of commuting expansive integer matrices.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Chiera, Taoufik Safer

item.title: Feynman integrals, coactions and Lie-algebra representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.26679v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We outline a link between canonical differential equations of Feynman integrals and matrix representations of flat connections taking values in certain Lie algebras. Leveraging insights from string theory and properties of periods associated with these Lie algebras, we deduce single-valued solutions to the differential equations and coactions for the integrals. We introduce a novel form of the differential equations which connects with the representation theory of the Lie algebras and may depart from $\varepsilon$-factorisation in a controlled way. We illustrate the formalism through relevant examples.
item.dc:creator: Emiel Claasen, Mehregan Doroudiani, Claude Duhr, Axel Kleinschmidt, Franca Lippert, Oliver Schlotterer, Yoann Sohnle

item.title: Planar cut-and-project sets with interval windows are bi-Lipschitz equivalent to lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.26707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose window is a line segment is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice: if $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3$ is a plane which is not spanned by vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^3$, $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$, and $\sigma$ is a segment of any length which is transverse to $V$, then the set of points $v\in V$ with $v+x\in\sigma+\mathbb{Z}^3$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to $\mathbb{Z}^2$. For planes of Diophantine slope this is a theorem of Burago and Kleiner, and the point of the present paper is that no Diophantine condition on the plane is needed. We also show that the same conclusion holds when the window is a finite union of intervals. Together with the author's construction of a cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window of countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to any lattice, this shows that for planes in $\mathbb{R}^3$ the answer to the bi-Lipschitz question depends on the shape of the window rather than on the Diophantine properties of the plane.
item.dc:creator: Alan Haynes

item.title: Partial sums of Rogers-Ramanujan functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.26719v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Explicit positive multisums on base q^5 for the Rogers-Ramanujan sum function and its partial sum are given. 32 combinatorial interpretations for these identities are given. The classical mod 5 Rogers-Ramanujan identities are recovered as a limiting case. These results are equivalent to a quintic basic hypergeometric identity.
item.dc:creator: Dennis Stanton

item.title: An Infinite Family of Overpartition Congruences Modulo 1944
item.description: arXiv:2611.26943v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\overline p(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$. We prove that $\overline p(16^\alpha(96n+76))\equiv0\pmod{1944}$ for all nonnegative integers $\alpha$ and $n$, extending the congruence for $\overline p(96n+76)$ established by Smoot. The key step is a three-term congruence modulo $243$ relating $\overline p(m)$, $\overline p(16m)$, and $\overline p(256m)$ for $m\equiv4\pmod6$. We derive this relation and the two initial congruences using theta-function dissections. A separate theta-series argument establishes divisibility by $8$.
item.dc:creator: Li Zhang

item.title: Period maps and the $C_{\rm st}$ conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.27054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a family of elliptic curves over an open disc whose total space violates the $C_{\mathrm{st}}$ conjecture in degree $1$. Hence the conjecture, known for proper and for Stein varieties, as well as for products of such, does not extend to proper families over Stein bases. This is an instance of a general criterion: the $C_{\mathrm{st}}$ conjecture holds for the total space of a smooth proper family over a sufficiently small open disc if and only if its period map is constant, i.e., all Gauss--Manin Higgs fields vanish or, equivalently, the $p$-adic local systems $R^if_*\mathbf{Q}_p$ are geometrically constant. This criterion is special to curves: over a $2$-dimensional polydisc, we give a family of $p$-adic analogues of non-K\"ahler elliptic surfaces whose period maps and local systems are constant, but whose total space violates the conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Colmez, Wies{\l}awa Nizio{\l}, Xinyu Shao

item.title: Linear support bounds for supercuspidal matrix coefficients of p-adic groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.27688v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}$ be a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. For any standard congruence tower $K_{\bullet}=(K_n)$ in $\mathbf{G}(F)$, supercuspidal matrix coefficients between $K_n$-fixed vectors are supported in an adjoint ball of radius $an+b_{K_{\bullet}}$, compact modulo the center, with $a$ depending only on $F$ and $\mathbf{G}$. When $\mathbf{G}(F)$ is non-compact modulo its center, the linear dependence on $n$ is optimal. In algebraic families we obtain a uniform radius $An+Bk+C+\operatorname{val}_{F}(N)$, where $k$ bounds the logarithmic height of the parameter. We deduce a sharp linear bound for the exponent in Bernstein's stabilization theorem. For quasi-split classical groups, we also remove the dyadic level restriction in the limit multiplicity theorem.
item.dc:creator: Itay Glazer, Erez Lapid, Zhengyu Mao, Mark Shusterman

item.title: Calabi-Yau fibrations and orbifold Mordell
item.description: arXiv:2611.27727v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct isotrivial projective families of Calabi-Yau varieties with arbitrarily large inf-multiplicities and no divisible fibres over the projective line. As an application, we show that any single instance of Campana's Orbifold Mordell Conjecture for a general-type C-pair of genus at most one (with only finite multiplicities) implies that the Weakly Special Conjecture is false.
item.dc:creator: Ariyan Javanpeykar

item.title: Boundary of the Lagrange and Markov spectra near Hall's ray
item.description: arXiv:2611.27731v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Lagrange and Markov spectra, denoted by $L$ and $M$, respectively, are closed subsets of the real line with intricate fractal geometry related to Diophantine approximations. In 1975, Freiman proved that both spectra contain the ray $[c_F,\infty)$, where $c_F=4.527829566\dots$, and that this ray is optimal, as both spectra avoid a tiny interval $(\nu_F,c_F)$. Using renormalization techniques and the thickness of Cantor sets, we prove that the boundaries $\partial L$ and $\partial M$ have positive Hausdorff dimensions arbitrarily close to $\nu_F$. Furthermore, in connection with Berstein's conjecture, which predicts that $[4.1,4.52]\subset L$, we exhibit a gap in $L$ near $4.08$, the first known gap in the region $L\cap[3.945,4.52]$. We also prove that the boundaries of both spectra have positive Hausdorff dimension near $4.5213$ and $4.08$.
item.dc:creator: Harold Erazo, Carlos Matheus, Carlos Gustavo Moreira

item.title: Kneser-Tits over fields of cohomological dimension $\le 2$ (with an appendix by Alexis Bouthier and Federico Scavia)
item.description: arXiv:2611.27803v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We settle the Kneser-Tits problem over every field $k$ of (separable) cohomological dimension $\le 2$, thus resolving a conjecture of Gille. More precisely, for such a $k$ and a semisimple, simply connected $k$-group $G$ whose indecomposable factors over $k$ are isotropic, we show that $G(k)$ is generated by "elementary matrices" (the $k$-points of the unipotent radicals of the parabolic $k$-subgroups of $G$), in other words, that $K_1^G(k) \cong 1$. In fact, we show this vanishing already when $k$ has separable $p$-dimension $\le 2$ in the sense of Gille with respect to a subset of the torsion primes $p$ of $G$, and we reinterpret the separable $p$-dimension itself via syntomic cohomology. To approach those $G$ that escape the net of previously known cases, for an inclusion of reductive $k$-groups $M \subset L$, we develop a new method based on the Rost invariant for transferring $R$-equivalence on $L/M$ to $R$-equivalence on $L$. To find homogeneous spaces to which our method fruitfully applies, we use the theories of prehomogeneous vector spaces and of special symplectic representations: concretely, for a $32$-dimensional half-spin representation $V$, we argue that the vectors in its unique open orbit $O \subset V$ admit unique up to interchange decompositions into sums of two pure spinors, and show that various double covers of $O$ built from such decompositions are rational varieties over any base field.
item.dc:creator: Kestutis Cesnavicius

item.title: On the chromatic splitting conjecture in coheight $1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.27879v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This article confirms predictions made by Hopkins' chromatic splitting conjecture in stable homotopy theory. A consequence of our main theorem is that a certain map of $K(h-1)$-local $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-rings $\mathbb{S}_{K(h-1)}^{B\mathbb{Z}}\to L_{K(h-1)}\mathbb{S}_{K(h)}$ admits a retract, so long as $p-1$ does not divide $h-1$. If $h=2$ and $p$ is odd, we show this map is an isomorphism. We use methods from the theory of $p$-divisible groups and $p$-adic geometry. Along the way we prove an entirely new kind of "two-tower isomorphism," in analogy with Faltings' isomorphism between the Lubin--Tate and Drinfeld towers, which parametrizes $p$-divisible groups over characteristic $p$ perfectoid spaces with fixed generic fiber in terms of negative Banach--Colmez spaces. Using the two-tower isomorphism, we gain control over the continuous cohomology of the Morava stabilizer group $\mathbb{G}_h$ with coefficients in $\pi_*L_{K(h-1)}E_h$. To study the continuous action of $\mathbb{G}_h$ on $L_{K(h-1)} E_h$, it was necessary to develop the theory of solid Lubin--Tate spectra. Adapting Lurie's constructions, we attach a solid Lubin--Tate spectrum to $p$-divisible groups over a broad class of solid rings in characteristic $p$.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Barthel, Lucas Mann, Rin Ray, Tomer M. Schlank, Andrew Senger, Jared Weinstein, Xinyu Zhou

item.title: Monodromy groups of Jacobians with definite quaternionic multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2303.00804v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a number field. The connected monodromy field of $A$ is the minimal field over which the images of all the $\ell$-adic torsion representations have connected Zariski closure. We show that for all even $g \geq 4$, there exist infinitely many geometrically nonisogenous abelian varieties $A$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ of dimension $g$ where the connected monodromy field is strictly larger than the field of definition of the endomorphisms of $A$. Our construction arises from explicit families of hyperelliptic Jacobians with definite quaternionic multiplication.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Cantoral-Farf\'an, Davide Lombardo, John Voight

item.title: Unlikely intersections in Shimura varieties and beyond: a survey
item.description: arXiv:2506.02900v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The aim of this note is to provide a concise introduction to so-called problems of unlikely intersections for (pure) Shimura varieties and to review the current state-of-the-art. In the process, we will touch upon more general settings and some of the results in those contexts.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Daw

item.title: Bilinear forms with Kloosterman fractions and applications
item.description: arXiv:2601.00292v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish bounds for bilinear forms $\sum\sum_{m,n}\alpha_m\beta_n\,e(a\overline{m}/n)$ with Kloosterman fractions, where $M<m\le 2M$, $N<n\le 2N$ and $(m,n)=1$, for arbitrary sequences of complex numbers $(\alpha_m)$ and $(\beta_n)$ and for positive integer numerators $a\ll X^{1/10}$, where $X=\max(M,N)$, and for the corresponding trilinear forms with an average over $a$. In the balanced case, where $M$ and $N$ are of the same order of magnitude, and for bounded $a$, the saving over the trivial bound is $X^{1/16-\varepsilon}$, which improves upon the savings $X^{1/48-\varepsilon}$ of Duke, Friedlander and Iwaniec and $X^{1/20-\varepsilon}$ of Bettin and Chandee. The proof follows the amplification method of these authors; where they apply Weil's bound, we use for most of the terms the estimates of Deshouillers and Iwaniec for sums of Kloosterman sums, in the form given by Pascadi. As an application, we prove an asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of the Riemann zeta-function with Dirichlet polynomials of length $T^{\theta}$ for $\theta<14/27$, extending the range $\theta<17/33$ of Bettin, Chandee and Radziwill. We also give applications to a determinant equation and to convolutions in arithmetic progressions with a fixed residue, on average over moduli as large as $x^{14/27-\varepsilon}$.
item.dc:creator: Anji Dong, Nicolas Robles, Dirk Zeindler

item.title: Explicit Formulas, Duality, and Periodicity for Multi-Indexed Poly-Bernoulli Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2603.15380v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study multi-indexed poly-Bernoulli numbers defined through multiple polylogarithms. The central result is an explicit formula in terms of Stirling numbers of the second kind and multinomial coefficients, valid in arbitrary depth and for arbitrary integral upper indices. We present a direct coefficient-extraction proof of the formula and derive the duality relation for negative upper indices from a symmetric multivariate exponential generating function. We then use these formulas to establish congruence periodicity in each lower index modulo an arbitrary prime power, extending the double-indexed result of Baba, Nakasuji, and Sakata. A second application gives a congruence for the sum over one complete period in the first lower index.
item.dc:creator: Yuna Baba, Tomoko Kikuchi, Maki Nakasuji

item.title: Arboreal Galois Groups of a PCF Map with Strictly Pre-periodic Critical Points
item.description: arXiv:2605.22466v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the arithmetic and geometric iterated monodromy groups associated to the postcritically finite (PCF) quadratic rational function $f(x)=\frac{2}{(x-1)^2}$ defined over a number field $k$, whose critical points are both strictly pre-periodic. We give explicit recursive descriptions of the topological generators of the geometric iterated monodromy group of $f$ and show that the arithmetic iterated monodromy group has Hausdorff dimension zero. We describe an explicit criterion to determine the values $a \in k$ for which the associated arboreal Galois group achieves its maximum possible size. In particular, we show that maximality of the arboreal Galois group can already be verified at level four, which is computationally accessible. We also determine the normalizer of the geometric IMG of $f$ and show that the arithmetic IMG equals the normalizer if $\zeta_8$ is not contained in $k$. Finally, we show that when $k=\mathbb{Q}$, the constant field contains $\mathbb{Q}(\mu_{2^{\infty}})$, providing the first full study of a PCF quadratic map with non-abelian constant field.
item.dc:creator: \"Ozlem Ejder, Zofia Go{\l}aska, Yasemin Kara, Leonie Nienhaus, \"Ozge \"Ulkem

item.title: The difference of the sums of odd and even parts of restricted partitions
item.description: arXiv:2606.16585v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a subset $D \subset \mathbb{N},$ denote by $S\!\left(D,n\right)$ the total sum of all odd parts minus the sum of all even parts of all partitions of $n$ in which parts from $D$ do not repeat. In this paper, we derive the generating function for $S\!\left(2\mathbb{N},n\right)$ and use it to give some congruences modulo 4. We also derive the generating function for $S\!\left(2\mathbb{N}-1,n\right)$ and give three congruences for these functions, one of which was previously proved by Garvan and Sarma.
item.dc:creator: Kilian Rausch, Johann Stumpenhusen

item.title: Zeta-regularization and natural boundaries: Sums and products of integers and primes
item.description: arXiv:2606.24536v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Euler regularized the divergent product of all positive integers and found beautiful formulas for regularized sums of integer powers of positive integers. These derivations essentially relied on what is now called the zeta-regularization technique, although analytical continuation had not yet been invented. This classic method is however not applicable to the product of all primes, as the prime zeta function has a natural boundary along the imaginary axis. Mu\~noz Garc\'ia and P\'erez-Marco overcame this obstacle and evaluated the product of all primes to $4\pi^2$ by finding an appropriately regularized value of the derivative of the prime zeta function at the origin, lying on the natural boundary. Their approach heavily relies on the M\"obius function and could therefore be called a M\"obius regularization. We extend this approach in two novel directions. First, we show how to make sense of the sum of all primes. This regularization requires going a finite distance beyond the natural boundary. Second, we determine the regularized products of integers and primes in the nine imaginary quadratic fields where integers have a unique factorization into primes, and establish a general power-law relationship between products of integers and primes. Two well-known examples are Gauss and Eisenstein integers. The interest in this approach goes beyond number theory. In a variety of physical situations, the zeta-regularization technique is indeed not applicable because the relevant zeta function has a natural boundary.
item.dc:creator: P. L. Krapivsky, J. M. Luck

item.title: The Gauss periods and cyclotomic matrices involving Gauss sums over cyclic groups
item.description: arXiv:2607.02392v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, by using the arithmetic properties of the Gauss periods and character sums over cyclic groups, we study the cyclotomic matrix $$A_k(\chi)=\left[G_N(\chi^{ki+ki})\right]_{0\le i,j\le \varphi(N)/k-1},$$ where $N=p^m$ is a prime power, $\varphi(\cdot)$ is the Euler totient function, $k$ is a divisor of $\varphi(N)$, $\chi$ is a generator of character group $\widehat{(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^{\times}}$, and $$G_N(\chi^{ki+kj})=\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}}\chi^{ki+kj}(x)e^{2\pi ix/N}$$ is the Gauss sum over $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Han Ji, Li-Yuan Wang, Hai-Liang Wu

item.title: A Unified Framework for $p$-adic Congruences and $p$-adic Interpolations of Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.11648v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we treat the problem of determining, for a fixed prime $p$, a positive integer $\ell$ that is coprime to $p$, and a real number $r$, when a sequence $\{c_n\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$ with the exponential generating function $F(t)$ satisfies the congruence $c_{n+\ell p^k}\equiv c_n \pmod{p^{k+r}}$ for all $k\ge0$ and large $n$ depending on $k$. Though this type of congruence is often observed for several number-theoretic or combinatorial sequences, such as Bernoulli numbers, Euler numbers, and Fibonacci numbers, it appears that their congruences have been shown individually. Traditionally, it is known that sequences derived as moments of $p$-adic measures satisfy stronger congruences. In this paper, instead of using $p$-adic measures, we investigate an algebraic structure of the set of generating functions and establish some conditions on $F(t)$ that are equivalent to or sufficient for the congruence and smoothness of the interpolating functions. This framework is an extension of the special case of $p$-adic moment sequences and provides a uniform manner to check the congruences $c_{n+\ell p^k}\equiv c_n \pmod{p^{k+r}}$ of concrete sequences. As an application, we also provide some equivalent conditions of the definition of Wall-Sun-Sun primes, also called Fibonacci-Wieferich primes.
item.dc:creator: Yuta Nishibuchi

item.title: Large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials and trilinear sums over short intervals
item.description: arXiv:2610.18923v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, Matom\"{a}ki, Pandey, Pliego, Ter\"{a}v\"{a}inen and Wang improved the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate of trilinear sums over short intervals of length $x^{\theta}$, which naturally reduces to estimating mean values of products of three Dirichlet polynomials. Based on recent works of Guth and Maynard and Chen, Gupta and Li on new large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials, they improved the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate for $\theta > \frac{3}{5}$. In this paper, we use their method to improve the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate for every $\frac{1}{2} < \theta < 1$. Our result yields improvements on many problems, including the work of Li on primes in short intervals of length $x^{0.52}$.
item.dc:creator: Runbo Li

item.title: The $\mathbb Q$-gonality of $X_1(42)$ is $12$
item.description: arXiv:2611.13155v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $\mathbb Q$-gonality of the modular curve $X_1(N)$ is known for all $N\le 40$ by work of Derickx and van Hoeij. We prove that the $\mathbb F_5$-gonality and the $\mathbb Q$-gonality of $X_1(42)$ are both $12$. The upper bound $12$ was already known, and we raise the previous lower bound from $10$ to $12$. Since the set of rational points of the Jacobian, $J_1(42)(\mathbb Q)$, is finite, it follows that $12$ is the least degree in which $X_1(42)$ has infinitely many points. The lower bound comes from an exhaustive search over Riemann--Roch spaces on $X_1(42)$ over $\mathbb F_5$, following Derickx and van Hoeij. We reduce this search by the orbits of a cyclic group of automorphisms of order $12$ on places of degree at most $5$. This leaves $743\,231$ Riemann--Roch spaces, about a quarter of the number needed by the earlier method. We prove the reductions and provide the code and data needed to reproduce the computations.
item.dc:creator: Sourajyoti Maiti

item.title: The monogenicity of $\boldsymbol{x^n+c\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}a^{n-j-1}x^j}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.20332v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We say that a monic polynomial $f(x)\in {\mathbb Z}[x]$ is {\em monogenic} if $f(x)$ is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$ and $\{1,\theta,\theta^2,\ldots,\theta^{{\rm deg}(f)-1}\}$ is a basis for the ring of integers of ${\mathbb Q}(\theta)$, where $f(\theta)=0$. Let $n,a,c\in {\mathbb Z}$ with $n\ge 3$, and suppose that \[{\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x):=x^n+cx^{n-1}+acx^{n-2}+a^2cx^{n-3}+\cdots +a^{n-2}cx+a^{n-1}c\] is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$. Recently, Jakhar, Kalwaniya and Yadav have given necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$, under the assumption that all prime divisors of the discriminant of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ not dividing $ac$ also do not divide $n+1$. In this note, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ without this restriction.
item.dc:creator: Lenny Jones

item.title: Cyclic Self-Dual Codes over Prime-Square Rings and Unimodular Lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.24153v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an explicit construction of cyclic Euclidean self-dual codes over $\mathbb{Z}/p^{2}\mathbb{Z}$, where $p$ is an odd prime, and use Construction~A to obtain unimodular lattices with large minimum norms. The construction is based on reciprocal factorizations of $x^n-1$. We explicitly describe the associated residue and torsion codes and analyze the relationship between minimum Euclidean weights and lattice minimum norms. We construct a unimodular lattice of minimum norm~$4$ in dimension~$49$, unimodular lattices of minimum norm~$5$ in dimensions $53$, $55$, $58$, $59$, and~$61$, and extremal unimodular lattices of minimum norm~$6$ in dimensions $69$ and~$71$. Using shadow theory and harmonic theta series, we prove that extremal unimodular lattices do not exist in dimensions $59$ and~$61$. Together with the known upper bounds, these results establish the optimality of the constructed lattices in all eight dimensions. In particular, we determine the previously unknown optimal minimum norms of unimodular lattices in five dimensions: $53$, $55$, $61$, $69$, and~$71$. We further construct unimodular lattices whose minimum norms are exactly one below the corresponding extremal bounds in dimensions $62$, $63$, $65$, $67$, $70$, $89$, $91$, $92$, $93$, and~$94$.
item.dc:creator: Minjia Shi, Mengru Yang, Patrick Sol\'e

item.title: On Hilbert's tenth problem over quadratic fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.25002v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2026, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. In this paper we study Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the quadratic fields $\mathbb Q(\sqrt2),\mathbb Q(\sqrt3),\mathbb Q(\sqrt6)$. Let $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)$ with $d\in\{2,3,6\}$. We prove that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{48})=0$ with integer coefficients whether it has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{48}\in K$. We also show the existence of a polynomial $f(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{25})$ with integer coefficients such that $a\in K$ is a rational integer if and only if $f(a,x_1,\ldots,x_{25})=0$ for some $x_1,\ldots,x_{25}\in K$.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Sun

item.title: Certified pandigital approximations of $\pi$, $\gamma$, $\delta$ and $e$
item.description: arXiv:2611.25358v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2004 Erich Friedman asked for the best approximations of $\pi$, $e$, the Euler-Mascheroni constant $\gamma$ and Feigenbaum's constant $\delta$ that use each of the digits $1, \dots, n$ exactly once, with addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, parentheses and the decimal point. We determine the optimal expressions for $\pi$, $\gamma$ and $\delta$ for every $n \le 9$, with the digits in any order and in increasing order, and for $e$ when $n \le 6$. The optima are found by exhaustive search and certified by an independent algorithm that encloses every expression rigorously and decides each candidate with Arb and exact arithmetic; a second certified computation covers intermediate values of any size. Twenty-one entries improve the records published before this work; one of them, the optimal formula for $\pi$ with 1-9 (error $2.81 \cdot 10^{-14}$), was found independently by M. Verheyen, and we prove it optimal. For $e$, whose records come from identities between power towers, we prove that Bamberger's formula is optimal within the natural family of such identities. All code and certificates are public.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Bendjema Garcia

item.title: An Eisenstein--Kronecker Modular Symbol and Beilinson--Kato Distributions
item.description: arXiv:math/0611704v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a $\G(\Q)$-modular symbol $\Phi$ from products of Eisenstein--Kronecker series by holomorphic projection modulo Eisenstein series. Its finite-level specializations recover the Borisov--Gunnells maps after a finite Fourier transform and polynomial duality. We reconstruct $\Phi$ by applying local explicit reciprocity to the ordered Siegel units defining the Beilinson--Kato distribution of Busuioc, Park, Patashnick, and Stevens. In weight $k\ge4$, rational torus covariance and the Manin relations determine the entire symbol in that weight from partial Fourier data for the coefficients of $X^{k-2}$ and $Y^{k-2}$. The cyclic Manin relation also has a geometric consequence. For every odd prime $p$, its weight-two equations, after elimination of the weight-two coordinates, cut out the modular curve $X(p)$ scheme-theoretically in weight-one Eisenstein coordinates. At level one its coefficients give all linear relations among unordered products of two Eisenstein series.
item.dc:creator: Vicen\c{t}iu Pa\c{s}ol

item.title: Stratification de Hesselink rationnelle et contribution unipotente \`a la formule des traces en caract\'eristique p>0
item.description: arXiv:2212.03792v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a field $F$ and a connected reductive group $G$ defined over $F$, we develop a theory of Kempf-Rousseau-Hesselink unipotent $F$-strata in $G(F)$ that should allow us to attack open problems in positive characteristic. As an application, we use this theory to establish an expansion (preliminary to the fine expansion) of the unipotent contribution to the trace formula over a global field of characteristic $p>0$. The unipotent $F$-strata play here the role of the unipotent geometric orbits in Arthur's work over a number field. The expansion in terms of products of local distributions is not discussed here; it will be the subject of further work.
item.dc:creator: Bertrand Lemaire

item.title: Solvable points on intersections of quadrics, cubics, and quartics
item.description: arXiv:2508.00215v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not 2 or 3. We establish polynomial bounds on the ambient dimension $N$, such that if $N$ is at least as big as this bound, every intersection $X\subset\mathbb{P}^N$ of quadrics, cubics and quartics has a solvable point, and a general one has a dense collection of solvable points, i.e. points in $X(k^{\mathrm{Sol}})$ where $k^{\mathrm{Sol}}/k$ is a solvable closure. Our method connects the classical theory of polar hypersurfaces to Fano varieties $\mathcal{F}(j,X)$ of linear subspaces on $X$, and we use this to obtain improved control on the arithmetic of $\mathcal{F}(j,X)$
item.dc:creator: Claudio G\'omez-Gonz\'ales, Jesse Wolfson

item.title: An exceptional set of uniformly spread Kakutani tilings of the line
item.description: arXiv:2512.23079v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The $\alpha$-Kakutani substitution rule splits the unit interval into two subintervals of lengths alpha and $1 - \alpha$, for a fixed $\alpha \in (0,1)$. A simple inflation-substitution procedure produces tilings of the real line and their associated Delone sets. We show that there are precisely five distinct values of $\min(\alpha, 1 - \alpha)$ for which these sets are uniformly spread, meaning that they are a bounded displacement of a lattice. The proof of this surprising fact combines the construction and analysis of a related family of primitive substitution tilings, Solomon's criterion for uniform spreadness, and a classification of Pisot-Vijayaraghavan polynomials.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Yotam Smilansky. An exceptional set of uniformly spread Kakutani tilings of the line. Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems 61 (2027), p. 105565
item.dc:creator: Yotam Smilansky

item.title: The Bias Conjecture for One-Parameter, Non-Isotrivial Elliptic Curve Families
item.description: arXiv:2609.38664v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate Miller's bias conjecture for general one-parameter families of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with non-constant $j$-invariants. Utilizing methods developed by Michel, we view the second moment as the sum of distinct cohomological components: a main $p^2$ term, a $p^{3/2}$ term arising from the first cohomology over the projective line, and terms of order $p$ or lower corresponding to singular fibers. By assuming the generalized Sato-Tate conjecture, we employ representation and motive theory to demonstrate that the coefficient of the $p^{3/2}$ term averages to zero in the limit. We then independently analyze the lower-order contributions without assuming Sato-Tate. By applying the Chebotarev density theorem and analyzing Galois representations, we show that the contributions to the order $p$ term from additive singular fibers average to a non-positive value. Consequently, the only remaining average contribution to the $p$ term is $-B_pp$, where $B_p$ denotes the number of ``bad'' points where the discriminant vanishes. Because $B_p$ averages to a strictly positive value, the overall coefficient of the $p$ term averages to a strictly negative value in the limit, thereby establishing the bias conjecture for these families.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Chen, Joshua Im, Steven J. Miller, Devayani Pradhan

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
item.description: arXiv:2610.37423v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the sharp bound $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$ for the threefold additive energy of every lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, with an absolute constant. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ estimate for eigenfunctions on $\mathbb{T}^2$, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical uniform $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and confirms Bourgain's conjecture in this range. For all $k\ge4$, we obtain the fixed power saving for the $k$-fold additive energy $J_k(P_n)\le C|P_n|^{2k-3-\delta}$, with absolute constants $C,\delta>0$. Applications include mean-square convergence of observables and the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.
item.dc:creator: Guiyu Xie, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Convergence in law of the maximum of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
item.description: arXiv:2611.01905v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $T \to \infty$, let $\tau$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$, and let $\sigma = \sigma(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. We establish the convergence in law of the recentered maximum of $\log|\zeta(\sigma + \mathrm{i}\tau + \mathrm{i} h)|$ over $I_{\theta} = \smash{[ - (\log T)^{\theta},(\log T)^{\theta}]}$, for every fixed $\theta > 0$. Under explicit conditions on the displacement $\sigma - 1/2$, the recentered maximum converges to a Gumbel distribution with scale parameter $1/(2\sqrt{1 + \theta})$. The recentering is an exact upper quantile of the one-point law of the associated Haar field $F_{h}^{\mathrm{H}} = \Re\sum_{p^{j}\leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(jp^{j(\sigma + \mathrm{i} h)})$, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. The positive constant in the limiting distribution is characterized by a Gaussian process describing the limiting microscopic increments of the Haar field around a high point. The result is established without the Riemann hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Ouimet

item.title: Relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel of a reductive group over a global field
item.description: arXiv:2611.04773v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe an algorithm and a computer program computing the relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel $Sha^S(K,G)$ of a reductive group $G$ over a global field $K$ with respect to a finite set $S$ of places of $K$ containing no archimedean places. We assume that we know the algebraic fundamental group $\Lambda=\pi_1^{alg}(G)$ together with the action on it of the Galois group $\Theta=Gal(L/K)$, where $L/K$ is a finite Galois extension with no real places such that $Gal(K^s/L)$ acts trivially on $\Lambda$. We also assume that we know the decomposition subgroups $\Theta_v\subseteq \Theta$ for all places $v$ in $S$, and all non-cyclic decomposition subgroups $\Theta_v$ for $v$ outside $S$. Under certain conditions, we compute the set $Sha^S(K,G)$ also when $S$ contains archimedean places.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Borovoi
